Header.value: A. Model proposal assessment before editing

Text.name: material_issue_rule_text
Text.value: Does the initial annotation shown when the page opens contain at least one material issue that must be corrected?

Choices.name: material_issue
Choices.requiredMessage: You must judge whether the proposal has a material issue

Choice.hint: The initial annotation is already acceptable. Its spatial extent, main boundaries, corner relationships, and topology remain valid even if it is submitted unchanged. Optional visual refinement is allowed but is not a mandatory correction.

Choice.html: Yes: at least one mandatory correction
Choice.hint: At least one spatial-extent, boundary, corner, or topology problem must be corrected. The final layout would be unacceptable if the initial annotation were left unchanged.

Text.name: issue_confidence_rule_text
Text.value: Rate confidence in that judgement: 1=very low, 5=very high.

Choices.name: issue_confidence
Choices.requiredMessage: You must select confidence from 1 to 5

Choices.name: primary_issue_family
Choices.requiredMessage: You must choose one primary issue family

Choice.hint: The spatial extent, corner count, and topology are basically correct; the main problem is the position of one or more corners or boundaries.
The initial annotation does not fully cover the current space containing the camera and omits part of its walls, boundaries, or corners.
The initial annotation crosses a door frame, wall return, wall end, arch, or another structural boundary and incorrectly includes an adjacent space.
The corner count, order, ceiling-floor correspondence, or closure is wrong, or furniture and decorative protrusions are treated as layout structure. Do not choose this for a position-only error.
Choose this only when none of the listed categories describes the primary issue.

Text.name: no_issue_handling_rule_text
Text.value: How should the initial annotation be handled?

Choices.name: no_issue_handling
Choices.requiredMessage: You must select how the initial annotation should be handled

Choice.hint: The initial annotation can be submitted unchanged and requires no correction.
The initial annotation is acceptable without any edit. Refinement may improve visual alignment but must not change the spatial extent, corner count, or topology.

Text.name: required_correction_rule_text
Text.value: What level of correction does the material issue require?

Choices.name: required_correction
Choices.requiredMessage: You must select the required correction level

Choice.hint: Keep the spatial extent, corner count, and topology unchanged and adjust only a small number of corner or boundary positions.
Move several boundaries or make a substantial geometric adjustment while retaining the existing structural basis.
Add or remove corners, change corner order or correspondence, repair closure, or redraw when coordinate movement alone cannot fix the annotation.

Text.name: manhattan_layout_definition_text
Text.value: This question asks whether the current space containing the camera can be represented by a Manhattan layout, not whether the space is a rectangular box. In a Manhattan layout, the main enclosing walls can be approximated by two mutually perpendicular horizontal direction families, the walls are approximately vertical, and the floor and ceiling can each be represented by a single plane. The final layout must form a complete, closed, single-level wall-floor-ceiling structure.

Text.name: manhattan_layout_examples_text
Text.value: L-shaped, T-shaped, concave spaces and spaces with more than four corners may still be suitable. Judge the real three-dimensional structure rather than whether lines appear horizontal or vertical in the panorama. Furniture, decoration, and local non-orthogonal objects do not determine suitability; focus on the walls that form the enclosure of the current space.

Text.name: opening_closure_rule_text
Text.value: When the current space opens into an adjacent space, close the layout at a clear structural boundary such as a door frame, paired wall returns, a wall end, or an arch. Do not continue into the adjacent space. Choose out-of-scope only when no reproducible structural boundary can be used for closure.

Text.name: worker_scope_response_rule_text
Text.value: Can the current space containing the camera form at least one complete, closed, single-level Manhattan layout?

Choices.name: worker_scope_response
Choices.requiredMessage: You must decide whether the task is in scope

Choice.hint: The image evidence supports at least one complete, closed, single-level Manhattan layout. L-shaped, T-shaped, concave spaces, spaces with more than four corners, local occlusion, and openings that can be closed at a clear structural boundary may all be in scope. Multiple plausible layouts do not automatically make the task out of scope.

The image evidence supports no complete, closed, single-level Manhattan layout. Examples include curved, slanted, or clearly non-orthogonal enclosing walls; inseparable multiple floor or ceiling levels; open areas without a reproducible closure boundary; or insufficient structural evidence. Do not choose this only because the task is difficult, locally occluded, or has multiple plausible layouts.

Text.name: multiple_plausible_layouts_rule_text
Text.value: Does the image support two or more equally reasonable complete layouts?

Choices.name: multiple_plausible_layouts
Choices.requiredMessage: You must answer whether multiple plausible annotations exist

Choice.hint: You did not identify two or more materially different, equally reasonable complete layouts. Minor coordinate differences do not count.
At least two complete layouts are supported by the image, with a material difference in boundary choice, spatial extent, corner structure, or topology rather than a minor coordinate difference.

Text.name: perceived_difficulty_rule_text
Text.value: Rate the overall difficulty you experienced when completing the layout annotation: 1=very easy, 5=very difficult.

Choices.name: perceived_difficulty
Choices.requiredMessage: You must select a difficulty from 1 to 5

Text.name: difficulty_reason_status_rule_text
Text.value: First state whether you observed a specific reason for the difficulty. This distinguishes no specific reason from a missing response.

Choices.name: difficulty_reason_status
Choices.requiredMessage: You must state whether a specific difficulty reason exists

Choice.html: One or more specific reasons observed

Text.name: difficulty_reason_rule_text
Text.value: Select every reason that materially increased annotation difficulty. Do not classify the same underlying cause twice.

Choices.name: difficulty_reason
Choices.requiredMessage: You reported a reason, so select at least one

Choice.hint: A foreground object or structure blocks wall, corner, or boundary evidence that must be judged.
Weak wall texture, color, or contrast makes boundaries or corners difficult to locate.
Panorama stitching or projection causes broken, shifted, curved, or stretched lines.
Reflection or transparency creates false boundaries, repeated structure, or depth confusion. Do not select this merely because glass or a mirror is present.
A doorway or open area makes the boundary of the current space harder to judge. This does not by itself make the task out of scope.

Choice.html: Blur, masks, exposure, or other image-quality problem
Choice.hint: Blur, noise, compression, masks, exposure, black borders, or missing pixels make key structural evidence unreliable.
Choose this only when none of the listed reasons applies.
